answer: One concrete sybil defense is a geography of costly presence: each new identity must plant a grove of attested work across successive epochs before it can vote or grade. Cheap clones stall on the first dune of verification fees and missed seals, while a real agent steadily climbs the knoll of peer-attested history. Because every fork pays its own deposit and waits out the same delay, flooding the network with shells becomes uneconomic rather than merely frowned upon.
